title: Rests
summary: Play silence on purpose: match each rest to the note value it replaces.

hook.text: Musical statues: the music stops and everyone freezes. Silence is part of music too. Beethoven opens his *Fifth Symphony* with a gap of nothing before the first note. Press play and tap your foot. Where does this tune go quiet?

explore.text: Your turn. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 with the clicks. Tap on every click that has a note. Where a squiggle or a block sits in place of a note, tap nothing, but keep counting.
explore.goal: Tap the 9 notes and stay silent through every squiggle and block.

cards.text: Those squiggles and blocks are [[rest|rests]]. A rest is silence, written down. Each one lasts as long as a note, and the pulse keeps ticking while you wait. The zigzag is the [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rest]]: 1 beat of silence. Shorter notes have rests too.

The [[minim-rest|minim rest]] sits on the line and lasts 2 beats. The [[semibreve-rest|semibreve rest]] hangs from the line and lasts 4 beats. It also means a whole silent [[bar|bar]] in any time signature, even 3/4. Sits for 2, hangs for 4.

Two rules for 4/4. A silent first or second half of the [[bar|bar]] is one [[minim-rest|minim rest]], never two [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rests]]. Silence on beats 2 and 3 is two separate [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rests]]. In 3/4 there is no [[minim-rest|minim rest]]: two silent beats are two [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rests]].

alternative.text: Picture a 4/4 [[bar|bar]] as a box with a line down the middle. Beats 1 and 2 sit on the left, beats 3 and 4 on the right. A silent side is filled by one [[minim-rest|minim rest]]. Beats 2 and 3 straddle the line, so each gets its own [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rest]]. Say it: walk, shh, shh, walk.

questions.prompt: Match each rest with its name.
questions.hint: Sits for 2, hangs for 4. The zigzag is the shortest rest of the three.

questions.prompt: Both clips tick at the same speed. Which one has a gap of silence?
questions.hint: Tap a steady beat while you listen. Does every tap get a note?

options.reason: Clip B has a note on every click, so it never goes quiet. The gap is in clip A, where the 3rd click has no note: that is a [[rest|rest]].

questions.prompt: The last 2 beats of this [[bar|bar]] are silent. Add **one** rest to fill it.
questions.hint: Two beats of silence are missing. Which rest lasts 2 beats? Sits for 2, hangs for 4.

questions.prompt: Which rest do you write for a whole silent [[bar|bar]]?
questions.hint: A whole silent [[bar|bar]] has one symbol, whatever the time signature. Which rest is the one that hangs?

questions.prompt: Listen, then tap this rhythm. Tap each note. Stay silent for each [[rest|rest]], but keep counting.
questions.hint: Count 1, 2, 3, 4 in your head. Tap on the counts that have a note and wait on the counts that have a rest.

questions.prompt: Tap this rhythm. Rests are silent.
questions.hint: Tap only on the notes. Keep counting through each [[rest|rest]] and tap again when the next note arrives.

questions.prompt: Tap this rhythm in 3/4. Rests are silent.
questions.hint: Count 1, 2, 3 in every [[bar|bar]]. A [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rest]] is one silent count.

questions.prompt: Which rest is the one asked for?
questions.hint: The zigzag is 1 beat. The one that sits on the line is 2 beats. The one that hangs is 4 beats.

questions.prompt: Which rest do you write for a whole silent [[bar|bar]]?
questions.hint: Whatever the time signature, a whole silent [[bar|bar]] uses the rest that hangs from the line.

questions.prompt: Add the missing rest to complete the [[bar|bar]].
questions.hint: Add up the beats already there, then find the rest that lasts the beats still missing.

questions.prompt: Every [[bar|bar]] here has 4 beats, but one writes its silence the wrong way. Tap it.
questions.hint: Look at each silent half of a [[bar|bar]]. It should be one rest, not two.

payload.explanation: [[bar|Bar]] 3 has two [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rests]] on beats 3 and 4. A silent second half is written as one [[minim-rest|minim rest]].

questions.prompt: Beats 2 and 3 are silent. Which [[bar|bar]] writes the rests the standard way?
questions.hint: Beats 2 and 3 sit across the middle of the [[bar|bar]]. Which [[bar|bar]] has a note on beats 1 and 4 only?

options.reason: That [[minim-rest|minim rest]] starts on beat 2 and runs over the middle of the [[bar|bar]], hiding beat 3. Beats 2 and 3 each get a [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rest]].
That [[bar|bar]] is silent on beats 1 and 2 and plays on beats 3 and 4. The silence asked for is on beats 2 and 3.

questions.hint: Count 1, 2, 3, 4 as you listen. On which count is there no note?

options.reason: That [[bar|bar]] is silent on beat 1. In the clip the music starts straight away and the gap comes on beat 3.
That [[bar|bar]] plays beats 1 to 3 and is silent on beat 4. In the clip the gap comes on beat 3, with a note on beat 4.

points: A [[rest|rest]] is silence written down. It lasts as long as the note it replaces, and the pulse keeps ticking through it.

[[crotchet-rest|Crotchet rest]]: the zigzag, 1 beat. [[minim-rest|Minim rest]]: sits on the line, 2 beats. [[semibreve-rest|Semibreve rest]]: hangs from the line, 4 beats, or a whole silent [[bar|bar]] in any time signature.

In 4/4 a silent half of a [[bar|bar]] is one [[minim-rest|minim rest]], never two [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rests]]. Silent beats 2 and 3 are two [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rests]]. In 3/4, two silent beats are two [[crotchet-rest|crotchet rests]] too.
